videos.title: Nie czekaj, aż życie postawi przed Tobą wyzwanie
videos.description:
Większość ludzi czeka, aż życie postawi przed nimi jakiś problem, zmusi ich do zmiany albo podrzuci okazję, której nie sposób przeoczyć. 

Tymczasem człowiek świadomy nie musi czekać na trudności, ponieważ potrafi samodzielnie wymyślać wyzwania, które uczynią jego życie ciekawszym, bogatszym i bardziej wartościowym. 

Ale żeby zacząć świadomie wybierać własne wyzwania, trzeba najpierw zrobić coś, czego wielu ludzi skutecznie unika - zacząć naprawdę myśleć! 

Podczas kolejnego Klubu 555 porozmawiamy o tym, dlaczego tak łatwo przyzwyczajamy się do życia, jakie znamy, i jak obudzić w sobie odwagę do stawiania pytań, które mogą zmienić naszą przyszłość. 

Bo być może największym wyzwaniem, jakie możesz sobie dzisiaj postawić, jest przestać żyć wyłącznie z przyzwyczajenia i zacząć świadomie projektować własne życie!

O 5:55 kolejna kompetencja nowoczesnego człowieka

Ściskam!

Fryderyk

videos.title: Od odwagi spojrzenia w lustro do mądrości zmieniania siebie.
videos.description:
Większość ludzi uważa, że potrafi myśleć, ale znacznie mniej osób potrafi zakwestionować własne przekonania. 

Przez ostatnie dni w Klubie 555 uczyliśmy się patrzeć na siebie bez filtrów, dostrzegać własne sukcesy, wyciągać wnioski z błędów i przyjmować informacje, których nie zawsze chcemy słuchać. 

Dzisiaj połączymy te umiejętności w jedną z najważniejszych kompetencji dojrzałego człowieka - gotowość odkrywania prawdy, nawet gdy jest niewygodna. 

Zastanowimy się, dlaczego nasz umysł tak często woli bronić dotychczasowych przekonań, zamiast poszukiwać rzeczywistości. 

Bo prawdziwa mądrość zaczyna się nie wtedy, gdy potrafisz udowodnić, że masz rację, lecz wtedy, gdy potrafisz uczciwie przyznać, że mogłeś się mylić.

O 5:55 podsumowanie tygodnia

Ściskam!

Fryderyk

videos.title: A61 Dlaczego nigdy nie powtórzysz tego samego eksperymentu 2 razy? Fizyka przewidywania przyszłości
videos.description:
#JanKuban #pafere #FizykaŻycia
👉👉👉 https://patronite.pl/pafere 👈👈👈

Czy można przewidzieć zachowanie człowieka, tak jak oblicza się rozciągnięcie zwykłej sprężyny? W tym odcinku audiobooka Fizyka Życia Johna Freeslowa wchodzimy w fascynujący świat systemów, procesów i matematyki, która rządzi codziennością! 🧠⚙️   

Dowiedz się, jak z prostych obserwacji wyciągać reguły pozwalające przewidywać przyszłość – od budowy drzew w lesie, przez dziedziczenie cech i rozkład normalny, aż po ludzkie charaktery i reakcje na kryzys. Zobaczysz też, dlaczego w prawdziwym świecie żaden eksperyment nie jest w 100% powtarzalny oraz czym różni się system stabilny od niestabilnego, w którym najmniejszy błąd zmienia wszystko. 📉📈   

W tym odcinku (rozdziały 3.16 – 3.17.3) usłyszysz o:
🧲 Charakterystyce systemów: co łączy obciążoną sprężynę z przekornym dzieckiem?   
🧬 Charakterystyce modyfikacji: jak krzywa dzwonowa opisuje zmiany w przyrodzie.   
🎯 Procesach i celach: jak orzeł dolatuje do celu i dlaczego definicja z ekonomii wygrywa z matematyką.   
⚖️ Trzech rodzajach systemów: poznaj systemy stabilne, niestabilne i asymptotycznie stabilne (i sprawdź, którym z nich jesteś Ty!).   

Włącz odcinek, daj się wciągnąć w naukowe spojrzenie na rzeczywistość i napisz w komentarzu, czy w życiu bliżej Ci do „cienkiej rurki” stabilności, czy do nieprzewidywalnego chaosu! 👇🎧

videos.title: Morgins: najgorszy bikepark w Portes du Soleil?
videos.description:
Bike park Morgins w szwajcarskiej części Portes du Soleil to miejsce, do którego mimo wielu wizyt w tym regionie nigdy wcześniej nie dojechaliśmy. Zawsze wydawał nam się mniej ciekawy niż sąsiedzi, więc sprawdzamy, jak jest w rzeczywistości.

32 bikeparki, 4 tripy, jeden sezon.

To drugi przystanek naszego trzeciego tripa. Startujemy z Les Gets i zamiast objeżdżać góry samochodem, jedziemy do Morgins rowerami przez całe Portes du Soleil. Na miejscu jest kameralnie: mały parking w środku miasteczka i podczas naszego pobytu prawie nikogo na trasach.

Na mapie są dwie główne trasy, w tym jedna niebieska. Szybko okazuje się, że z łatwą trasą na rozgrzewkę ma niewiele wspólnego. Magda po pierwszym fragmencie wypycha rower z powrotem do góry, a ja zjeżdżam dalej sam. Jest wąsko, szybko i nierówno, w otwartym kasku nie czułem się tam komfortowo, a nagranie z GoPro zupełnie tego nie oddaje.

Nadzieję odzyskuję na trasie Toboggan, z pionowymi bandami, w których dobrze czuć przyczepność. Potem dołączam do ekipy Ride It: jadę za uczestnikami wyjazdu, a na koniec za instruktorami, już bez taryfy ulgowej.

Mój werdykt: to bike park dla downhillowców. Kiedy założyłem full face i zbroję, zrobiło się naprawdę fajnie. Dla początkujących i dla kogoś, kto szuka spokojnej niebieskiej trasy, będzie tu za trudno. Nie jest to bike park wybitny i nie jechałbym tak daleko tylko dla niego, ale można się tu dobrze pobawić.

Konkurs: do wygrania opona Continental Argotal w wersji enduro, 29 x 2,4. Pytanie pada pod koniec filmu, wygrywa pierwsza poprawna odpowiedź w komentarzu.

PARTNERZY

Dartmoor Bikes

Seria „Miejscówki” powstaje z Dartmoor Bikes.

Shimano Polska

Podczas jazdy korzystam z napędu i hamulców Shimano.

Dacia Duster

Samochód, którym ruszyliśmy w cztery tripy po europejskich bike parkach. Hybryda z LPG z napędem na cztery koła w wersji Extreme.

Konrad Kasprzyk, Phinance

Ja i cała ekipa Dirt It More jesteśmy ubezpieczeni u Konrada Kasprzyka.
https://sportowcy-phi.pl/?partnerId=dirtit

Ride It

Firma organizująca wyjazdy i szkolenia rowerowe. W Portes du Soleil zatrzymaliśmy się razem z ekipą Ride It, a w Morgins jeżdżę z uczestnikami i instruktorami ich wyjazdu.

https://dirtit.pl/

videos.title: Guilt Free: Why You're Done Living for Everyone Else with Dr. Jennifer Reid
videos.description:
Why do you feel guilty for everything, even when you've done nothing wrong?

In this book launch episode, psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Reid explains why so many women feel guilty around the clock, and how guilt is often covering up anger, grief, exhaustion, and other emotions underneath.

She breaks down her Guilt Equation and the Four Furies that keep the equation stuck:

1. Constant Caretaking
2. Hyper-Accountability
3. Seeking Perfection
4. Having It All

You'll also hear her SPEAK Framework in full: Showing Up, Paying Attention, Examining, Action, and Keep Going: a five-step practice for moving from guilt toward agency, including learning to delegate, disappoint people when needed, and set boundaries that let you stay connected without burning out.

In this episode, you'll learn:

- Why "if I don't feel guilty, I don't care" keeps you stuck
- Why perfectionism keeps moving the goalpost
- How to examine the expectations behind a guilty thought
- Why you may need to be willing to disappoint people to be free
- How to use SPEAK as a daily practice, not a one-time fix

What's one expectation you've been carrying that you're ready to put down? Tell me in the comments.

———

ABOUT DR. JENNIFER REID:

Dr. Jennifer Reid is a psychiatrist and the author of Guilt Free: Reclaiming Your Life from Unreasonable Expectations. In her work, she helps women identify the unreasonable expectations driving constant guilt, perfectionism, and people-pleasing and replace them with a more grounded, compassionate way of seeing themselves and their lives. She is the creator of the SPEAK Framework, a practical practice for noticing guilty thoughts, examining the expectations behind them, and taking action toward agency.

videos.title: Why We Self-Sabotage When Things Start Going Well
videos.description:
Why do we self-sabotage when things start going well?
Self-handicapping, impostor feelings, and fear of success can make good news feel threatening.

For deeper reflections, become a Patron of The Psyche. Read weekly written pieces, including a reflection on Jonah and Maslow:
https://www.patreon.com/ThePsyche

A missed deadline right after a promotion. An argument when a relationship is finally going well. These moments can look like bad luck or poor discipline, but sometimes they serve a hidden purpose: protecting us from the possibility that our best might not be enough.

In 1978, psychologists Steven Berglas and Edward Jones studied self-handicapping, finding that people who felt their success was undeserved could prefer an obstacle before their next test. That same year, Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes described the impostor phenomenon, helping explain why achievement and recognition can bring shame and fear of being exposed instead of confidence.

Abraham Maslow's Jonah complex, discussed in *The Farther Reaches of Human Nature* (1971), takes the question further. What if we fear not only failure, but also who we would have to become if we succeeded? We examine three familiar responses that can keep this pattern alive: bursts of motivation, endless planning, and lowering our goals. Then we look at what changes when we recognize the fear behind our reactions at work and in relationships.

Understanding these patterns is not the same as therapy. If they repeatedly cost you things that matter, speaking with a therapist is a legitimate step.

#SelfSabotage #FearOfSuccess #Psychology

videos.description:
There are seven levels of overthinking — and most people spend years stuck around level four without realizing there's a way out.

In this video, we break down exactly what's happening in your mind at each level: from the passing thought that drifts by, to the replay loops, the what-if spirals, the mind-reading, analysis paralysis, the physical toll — and the one level where overthinkers finally break free.

By the end, you'll know exactly which level you're on, how people stay stuck, how people move up, and the one question that cuts through all seven.

videos.title: Are You Abandoning Yourself to Keep Everyone Else Happy? | The People Pleasing Trap
videos.description:
Hosted by Heidi Hadley | Special Guest: Melanie Cool

Are you always putting everyone else's needs before your own?

Do you find yourself saying YES when you really want to say NO? Do you feel guilty when you take time for yourself? Are you constantly trying to keep everyone happy, even when it comes at the expense of your own happiness, health and wellbeing?

If this sounds familiar, you may be caught in the cycle of people-pleasing and self-abandonment.

In this thought-provoking episode of The Total Somatics Show, Heidi Hadley welcomes special guest Melanie Cool for an empowering conversation about the hidden cost of people-pleasing and the transformative journey towards self-awareness, self-respect and healthy boundaries.

Together, we explore an important question:

When does being kind, caring and supportive of others cross the line into abandoning ourselves?

For many of us, people-pleasing becomes such an automatic behaviour that we don't even realise we're doing it. We may have learned to prioritise other people's happiness, avoid conflict, seek approval or suppress our own needs to maintain harmony.

What happens when we spend so much time looking after everyone else that we lose connection with ourselves?

More importantly, how can we begin to change?

In this episode, we explore:

The hidden signs of people-pleasing: Recognising when kindness and generosity become patterns of self-sacrifice.
People-pleasing versus self-abandonment: Understanding when prioritising others means neglecting your own emotional, physical and psychological needs.
Why self-care isn't selfish: Discovering how honouring your own needs can help you become more present, balanced and connected in your relationships.
The journey towards self-awareness: Learning to recognise automatic behaviours, emotional triggers and deeply ingrained habits.
Creating healthy boundaries without guilt: Understanding that saying NO to something doesn't mean you're rejecting someone.
The nervous system and people-pleasing: Exploring how stress responses, including appeasement behaviours, may influence the way we interact with others.
The power of self-reflection: Becoming curious about your choices rather than judging yourself for past behaviours.
From people-pleasing to personal growth: Discovering how greater self-awareness, self-compassion and intentional choices can support lasting change.
Taking care of yourself is not selfish. It is an essential part of becoming whole.

videos.description:
Blisko 60% organizacji społecznych w Polsce zmaga się z brakiem następców, a praca liderek i liderów w stowarzyszeniach i fundacjach nierzadko wiąże się z ogromną odpowiedzialnością, samotnością na szczycie i ryzykiem wypalenia. Jak w świecie nieustannej presji odzyskać spokój, odwagę i przestrzeń na oddech?

Odpowiedzią bywa mentoring – relacja oparta na partnerstwie, zaufaniu i wzajemnej wymianie doświadczeń. O takiej właśnie relacji Magda Dobranowska-Wittels, redaktorka portalu ngo.pl, rozmawia z uczestniczkami projektu „Mosty Odporności” realizowanego przez Fundację Masz Moc:

Anettą Kietlińską (Centrum OPUS) – animatorką i doradczynią z ponad 20-letnim stażem, która dzieli się perspektywą mentorki,

Anną Ohirko (Stowarzyszenie Lokalni w Gminie Suchy Las) – prezeską i koordynatorką projektów, wnoszącą perspektywę lokalnej liderki.

🟠DLACZEGO WARTO OBEJRZEĆ ROZMOWĘ?

· Kiedy warto sięgnąć po mentoring i jakie sygnały mówią „Pora na wsparcie”?

videos.title: Men's Mental Health: Stop Waiting for Someone to Save You
videos.description:
November is Men's Mental Health Awareness Month, but how many people actually know that?

Men's mental health is something we talk about increasingly, yet suicide rates remain a devastating issue, male loneliness continues to be a concern, and too many men are struggling in silence.

In this episode of The Big Lad Podcast, I'm discussing why men's mental health deserves more attention, why simply telling men to open up might not be enough, and why purpose, friendship and human connection are so important.

I also explore why we need to stop waiting for other people to make the first move, why men need to feel useful and valued, and how taking small steps can make a significant difference.

We cover:
- Why Men's Mental Health Awareness Month deserves more recognition.
- The shocking differences between male and female suicide statistics.
- Why traditional approaches to mental health might not work for everyone.
- Why men need purpose and a sense of usefulness.
- The importance of finding the right therapist and not giving up after one bad experience.
- Why asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
- How loneliness and the decline of human connection are affecting us.
- Why making friends as an adult isn't as difficult as we sometimes think.
- The importance of checking in on your mates.
- Why you need to take action rather than waiting for somebody else.

One of the biggest messages I want people to take away from this episode is simple: you can come back from your worst days. You're still here, and things can get better.

If you're struggling, please don't suffer in silence. Speak to someone you trust, reach out to a support service or seek professional help. You don't have to figure everything out on your own.

UK support:
Samaritans – Call 116 123 (free, 24 hours a day).
Shout – Text SHOUT to 85258 for free, confidential text support.

If you're in immediate danger, call 999 or attend A&E.

videos.title: How to Start Freelancing When You're Not the Best at Anything
videos.description:
Starting an agency in India can make lakhs, but not if you sell everything for ₹35,000. Devrat, founder of Arise, explains what works instead.

Devrat has taken 4,800 documented sales calls since 2019, and he says one international client at $1,500 to $3,500 a month is already ₹1.5 to 3.5 lakh. In this conversation with Tanuj Verma he lays out the 4-step framework he would use to start an agency from zero: one service for one audience, a recurring monthly model, a daily outreach system, and a team smarter than the founder.

We also get into why most Upwork proposals get skipped (a job gets 40 to 50 of them, and the client reads the first two lines), his two-call close where the first call is a demo and the second is onboarding, why a client decides to stay or leave in the first 10 days, and why he refunds referral money instead of giving discounts. Near the end: who AI actually replaces, and his advice for an 18-year-old who wants to start an agency.

videos.title: Social Anxiety: How to Manage Overthinking and Enjoy Social Events
videos.description:
You want to have close friends. You want to feel connected to other people. You may even want to go out, meet new people, and enjoy social events. But when the opportunity comes, anxiety can make it feel almost impossible.

Maybe you spend days worrying about an upcoming event. You wonder what you will say, whether people will like you, or if you will embarrass yourself. Once you arrive, you become hyperaware of everything you do - how you look, what you say, where you are standing, and how others might be perceiving you. And when you get home, the overthinking may continue as you replay conversations and question whether you said or did something wrong.

Eventually, staying home can feel easier.

But avoiding social situations can come with its own cost. The more you avoid them, the more isolated and lonely you may feel. You may miss opportunities to build meaningful relationships, try activities you might enjoy, or simply experience the sense of connection you have been wanting.

When anxiety gets in the way of connection

Social anxiety is more than simply feeling shy or nervous around other people. For some people, the fear of being judged can become so overwhelming that socializing feels exhausting or even terrifying.

You might worry that others think you are strange or different. You might constantly compare yourself to everyone around you or assume that people are noticing your mistakes. Even when nothing goes wrong, your mind may search for evidence that you embarrassed yourself.

This can create a frustrating cycle: you want connection, but anxiety tells you to avoid the very situations where connection can happen.

Over time, that can leave you feeling lonely, bored, and unfulfilled - wondering why something that seems easy for other people feels so difficult for you.

What if socializing didn't feel so overwhelming?

Managing social anxiety doesn't mean you have to become the most outgoing person in the room or stop caring what other people think entirely. It can mean learning to recognize anxious thoughts, understand how they affect your behavior, and respond to them differently.

With greater awareness and the right tools, social situations can begin to feel more manageable. You may become more comfortable showing up as yourself rather than constantly worrying about how you are being perceived. videos.title: Why You Avoid the Things You Actually Love Doing | The Psychology of Self-Sabotage
videos.description:
**Topics Covered:** why you avoid things you love, psychology of procrastination, self-sabotage, fear of failure, perfectionism, emotional avoidance, motivation psychology, why you lose interest in hobbies, fear of success, overthinking, mental resistance, dopamine and motivation, anxiety and procrastination, human behavior, psychology of avoidance, self-improvement.

**About the Video:**

Have you ever wanted to do something so badly, yet somehow kept finding reasons not to do it?

Maybe you love drawing but haven't touched a pencil in months. You want to write, create videos, start a business, exercise, or work on a personal project. You think about it constantly, but when the moment comes to begin, you suddenly feel tired, distracted, overwhelmed, or unmotivated.

Why do we avoid the very things that make us happy?

The answer may be more complicated than laziness.

Sometimes, the things we love become connected to pressure, expectations, perfectionism, and the fear of disappointing ourselves. What once felt enjoyable starts feeling like another responsibility. And the more important something becomes to us, the harder it can feel to begin.

In this video, we explore the psychology behind emotional avoidance, self-sabotage, perfectionism, fear of failure, and the mental patterns that make us postpone the activities we genuinely care about.

You'll discover:

- Why enjoyable activities can start feeling like stressful responsibilities.
- How perfectionism makes starting difficult.
- Why fear of failure can hide behind procrastination.
- How overthinking destroys the excitement of creating.
- Why waiting for motivation keeps you stuck.
- How to reconnect with the things you genuinely love.

Because sometimes, the biggest obstacle between you and the life you want isn't a lack of passion. It's the psychological pressure you've unknowingly attached to that passion.

**Research & Psychological Concepts:**

This video explores psychological concepts including experiential avoidance, perfectionism, self-handicapping, fear of failure, intrinsic motivation, and procrastination. These concepts help explain why people sometimes avoid activities that matter deeply to them.

**Disclaimer:**

This video is for educational and informational purposes only. It explores general psychological patterns and is not intended to diagnose or treat mental health conditions. Individual experiences may differ.

videos.title: Wiesz, co robić, ale tego nie robisz. Oto dlaczego
videos.description:
Jak zacząć działać, pokonać własny opór i zbudować pewność siebie? Jeśli prokrastynacja, overthinking i strach przed oceną trzymają Cię w miejscu, czas przyjrzeć się swoim codziennym decyzjom. 🎯

Czytasz książki o rozwoju osobistym, oglądasz motywacyjne filmy, zapisujesz kolejne pomysły… a potem znowu odkładasz pierwszy krok. Czekasz na lepszy moment, większą pewność siebie albo dzień, w którym wątpliwości wreszcie znikną. Tylko co, jeśli właśnie to czekanie sprawia, że ciągle stoisz w miejscu?

🔥 W tym filmie rozkładam na części wewnętrzny opór przed działaniem. Omawiam wątpliwości, obawy przed oceną i ruminacje, czyli powracające rozmyślanie o tych samych sprawach. Pokazuję, jak patrzeć na własne ograniczenia, przestać odkładać wszystko na później i zacząć budować poczucie sprawczości poprzez konkretne zachowania.

Nie musisz czekać na idealny nastrój, żeby wykonać mały krok. Możesz zacząć od zadania, które jest wystarczająco proste, aby rzeczywiście je dokończyć. Pięć minut nauki, jeden umyty talerz, pierwszy fragment projektu — właśnie takie działania są punktem wyjścia do pracy nad samodyscypliną i zaufaniem do siebie.

🧠 OVERTHINKING I STRACH PRZED OCENĄ
Ile energii poświęcasz na wyobrażanie sobie, co pomyślą inni? Ile razy analizujesz możliwą porażkę, zanim w ogóle spróbujesz? W materiale przyglądam się temu, jak przewidywane konsekwencje i przekonania typu „nie mogę”, „nie mam” lub „nie jestem gotowy” wpływają na Twoje decyzje. Punktem wyjścia jest uczciwe uznanie obecnej sytuacji i wybranie następnego możliwego ruchu.

🎯 KORZYŚĆ, WPŁYW I KONTROLA
Przedstawiam trzy pytania, przez które możesz przepuścić swoje codzienne działania: czy to mi służy, na co mam wpływ i o czym mogę zdecydować? videos.title: *What If Self-Judgment Fuels Your Anxiety and Keeps You From Seeing How Strong You Are?

What if much of the anxiety you experience comes from believing the judgments you make about yourself?

Growing up, many of us learned that being accepted meant correcting something about ourselves. Get better grades. Stop being so sensitive. Try harder. Do better.

Over time, those messages can become an automatic way of thinking. And when someone questions our work, disagrees with us, or offers criticism, we don't just question what happened. We begin questioning ourselves.

But there's another side to this story.

Think about everything you've already navigated in your life. The disappointments, the struggles, the relationships that ended, and the moments when you weren't sure how you'd get through.

You did get through them.

In this episode of Beyond the Monkey Mind, JF Benoist explores how self-judgment fuels anxiety and disconnects us from the resilient person we've been all along.

You'll discover why trying to think your way out of anxiety can keep you stuck, and how becoming present with what you're actually feeling can open the door to a different relationship with yourself.

Because maybe the person you've been trying so hard to become is already here.

You don't have to become someone different to begin trusting yourself.

Dr. Christina Wilson examines how guilt around boundaries and suppressed emotions can distort faith, distinguishing biblical self-denial from self-erasure and codependency. Keywords


Christian boundaries, biblical self-denial, boundary guilt, honest prayer, Christian women, codependency, emotional vulnerability, spiritual health


Key Topics


How boundary guilt and suppressed vulnerability show up as spiritual misconceptions, particularly for women expected to be perpetual caretakers and peacekeepers.


The difference between biblical self-denial and complete self-erasure, and how emotional suppression and physical depletion can lead to burnout and bitterness.

Establishing limits is not a failure of love. It is an act of stewardship.


Jesus intentionally modeled healthy boundaries rather than yielding to constant public demand.


Jesus called us to lay down our lives for the gospel, not for the unreasonable expectations of others.


God cannot heal what you refuse to acknowledge.


Setting godly boundaries protects your capacity to love authentically rather than out of quiet resentment.


Raw vulnerability, not toxic positivity, is the mark of genuine faith.


Identify one non-essential commitment or request this week and decline it directly without offering an over-explained excuse or apologetic defense.


Write an unfiltered one-page letter to God. Lay out your unmet expectations, your hurts and frustrations without editing yourself for politeness.


Lord, I trust you with this reality.

videos.title: Gold Is 30% Off. I'm Still Not Buying.
videos.description:
📄 Free: 50 years of gold on one page. Every boom, every bust, and how long each lasted: https://the-efficient-life.kit.com/27c241ff5c

Gold fell to its lowest price in over a year this week, about 30% below the January high. A lot of people call that a buying opportunity. I own gold and I am not buying yet. A discount is not a plan. A price and a position size are. This video is my two levels, why I cap gold at a slice of the portfolio, and what I think you can do depending on how much gold you already own.

- My levels: I start adding at $3,800 and add heavily at $3,500. Set in the summer, not moved since. Gold is about $80 above the first one
- Central banks bought 321 tonnes in the third quarter, 42% more than a year earlier (World Gold Council). Coin and bar buyers are at a four-year low
- Gold lost about 4% a year from 1981 to 1999. A buyer at the 1980 top waited 28 years to get even, 45 after inflation
- Size: in my backtest the best result was gold at a fifth of the growth part of a portfolio. 30% and 40% were worse
- If I buy, the date and the price go in the pinned comment the same day

Most importantly, I break down three possible scenarios for the US economy and the key developments investors should watch on December 9th and 10th.

videos.title: Ibrahim Traoré's New Gold Backed African Currency: THE END OF CFA FRANC?
videos.description:
What if the money in your wallet was a ghost of colonialism? A symbol of control, lingering nearly 80 years after it was born. For decades, that’s been the heated debate around the CFA franc, a currency system born from the ashes of the French empire. But today, a new generation of military leaders in Africa’s Sahel region are threatening to finally exorcise that ghost.

This isn't just about printing new banknotes. It's a high-stakes rebellion. A confederation of three nations—Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger—is openly planning a radical break from the financial system that has tied them to Paris for decades. They’re proposing a new common currency, a move that could shatter France’s remaining influence and redraw the geopolitical map of West Africa.

But here’s the critical question: is this a real path to economic freedom, or a reckless gamble that could plunge roughly 75 million people into chaos? To get what's happening, you have to understand a story that starts with one of Africa’s most defiant leaders, a controversial plan for a gold-backed currency, and a dream many believe got him killed.

The West called him a dictator, but a powerful theory argues that Muammar Gaddafi was targeted for a different reason. He had a grand, audacious plan: to unite Africa with a single, gold-backed currency, a "gold dinar," that would have shattered the dominance of the U.S. dollar and the Euro in African trade. For many, this wasn't just a financial project; it was a declaration of economic independence.

Then, in 2011, came the NATO-led intervention in Libya. Gaddafi was overthrown and killed, and his dream of a gold dinar died with him. While the official reasons for the intervention were humanitarian, a persistent and powerful theory, found in leaked emails and widespread commentary, argues the real motive was to kill a threat to the global financial order. There's no conclusive proof for this claim, but the narrative has become a potent symbol across the continent. It’s a cautionary tale: challenge the system, and the system strikes back.

They thought that dream was buried in the Libyan desert. They might have been wrong. Today, a new generation of African leaders in the Sahel is picking up where Gaddafi left off. And their actions could finally bring an end to nearly 80 years of French financial architecture in Africa.

To get the scale of this rebellion, you have to understand the system they're rebelling against: the CFA franc.

videos.channel: Health, Reframed with Joel Rosen, DC
videos.description:
🧠 Start here (5-Day Brain Fuel Reset, $17) → https://courses.drjoelrosen.com/start

📄 Free: 7 Questions to Ask Before Believing a Health Claim → https://courses.drjoelrosen.com/research-brief
Joel Rosen, DC | MD Candidate. Education, not medical advice.

Everyone seems to be talking about nitric oxide and its role in circulation, cardiovascular health, and longevity. But another molecule involved in vascular regulation gets far less attention: endothelin-1 (ET-1).

In this episode of The Age Reversing Blueprint Podcast, I welcome back Morley Robbins, author of Cu-RE Your Fatigue and founder of the Root Cause Protocol, to explore the relationships between copper, iron metabolism, nitric oxide, endothelin-1, mitochondrial function, and cellular energy.

Morley shares his evolving perspective on how these biochemical systems interact and why he believes copper metabolism deserves greater attention.

But our conversation goes beyond copper.

After more than 25 years practicing chiropractic and functional medicine, I've returned to medical school, where I've developed an even greater appreciation for the complexity of human physiology.

Throughout this interview, we explore some important questions:

• What is endothelin-1, and how does it interact with nitric oxide in vascular regulation?
• How do copper and iron metabolism influence oxidative stress and cellular function?
• Could disruptions in these systems contribute to fatigue and metabolic dysfunction?
• Is copper overlooked in conventional medicine, or sometimes overemphasized in alternative medicine?
• What can ferritin, magnesium, and copper measurements actually tell us about physiological function?
• How can AI accelerate biochemical research while introducing hallucinations and confirmation bias?
• What role might BH4, nitric oxide synthase coupling, and oxidative stress play in neurological and psychiatric conditions?

One of the central themes of Health, Reframed is that understanding physiology requires moving beyond simple explanations. Copper may be important, but no single mineral, pathway, or molecule explains everything.

We must be conservative with our conclusions, not with our questions.

videos.title: What Happens When Fear Hits While the Future Keeps Getting Built
videos.description:
What happens when fear hits the market while the future keeps getting built.Nvidia announced Jensen Huang's resignation on November 12. He also left the board. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a successor. Nvidia fell about 2% Friday and posted a sixth consecutive weekly decline. Nvidia reports Tuesday.Bitcoin has broken below $65,000 and traded near $62,000. Bitcoin traded down to about $62,018 and then rebounded toward $65,000. Is crypto experiencing a final flush, or does the selling have further to go as a huge AI IPO approaches? Capitulation means holders are giving up and selling, often under pressure. Bitcoin needs to show it can hold a recovery after testing the low $62,000s.$65,000: Can Bitcoin reclaim this area and hold it?
$62,000 area: Does a retest attract buyers, or do sellers establish a new range below it?
$60,000: If the recent low fails, this is my next round-number reference.Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow with 825 million shares offered at an expected $70–$78. That implies roughly $57.8–$64.4 billion for the base offering, before the underwriters' option. Nasdaq lists November 19 as the expected trading date under ANT. Investors seeking an allocation may sell liquid holdings to fund it. Crypto is one place capital can be raised quickly, including over a weekend. Watch the expected Anthropic listing Thursday.For the week ended November 13, the S&P 500 gained 2.5% and the Nasdaq gained 2.3%. Friday itself was weaker, with the S&P down 0.4% and Nasdaq down 0.9%.Chip stocks have flashed a buying signal that one strategist is comparing with earlier market bottoms. A chip-stock rally of more than 17% over four days as a buying thrust. A four-day rally still needs follow-through before I call a durable bottom.Compute, data, and energy remain my framework. Compute determines how much AI you can run. Data influences what it can learn and do. Energy determines whether that infrastructure can operate at scale. Micron gives us exposure to the memory needed to feed AI workloads. Its high-bandwidth memory products connect the compute and data sides of the Power Triad. The Power Triad helps me look beyond one company, into data and the energy needed to run it all.The long-term thesis does not make every dip equally attractive. A lower quote can reflect a weaker business as well as an opportunity. Owning four chip stocks still leaves you exposed to a shared spending cycle.Assets covered: Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), Micron

videos.title: FULL PANEL: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh and Tech CEOs Debate AI's Future | AF15
videos.description:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh leads a major discussion on artificial intelligence, super intelligence and the future of the US economy at a conference hosted by the Federal Reserve Board and the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco on November 16, 2026.

Warsh examines whether rapid advances in AI could accelerate innovation, increase productivity and transform long-term economic growth. He discusses the potential impact on living standards, employment, financial markets and US competitiveness, while emphasizing that human judgment, responsibility and decision-making remain essential.

The panel features Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks; Patrick Collison, CEO of Stripe; and Max Levchin, CEO of Affirm. The technology leaders share how AI is changing their businesses, improving engineering productivity, enabling new companies and accelerating the development of products and services.

The discussion also explores the risks of AI-powered cyberattacks, vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure, the future of employment and the challenges facing companies as they adopt increasingly autonomous AI systems. The panelists consider whether the United States is moving ahead of other economies in AI development and adoption, and how technological advances could reshape global economic competition.

Warsh outlines several possible economic scenarios, including broad productivity gains, labor-market disruption and the risk that major AI investments may not deliver expected returns. The central question: can super intelligence usher in a new era of American economic growth?

Watch the full panel discussion on DWS News for insights into AI, the Federal Reserve, technology, cybersecurity and the future of the global economy.

videos.title: Schizophrenia or Demonic Possession? Psychotherapist's Shocking Claims: Jerry Marzinsky
videos.description:
Is schizophrenia simply a mental illness, or could there be something more mysterious behind the voices people hear?

In this episode of the Truth Theory Podcast, Mike Sygula speaks with Jerry Marzinsky, a retired licensed psychotherapist with over 35 years of experience working with people diagnosed with schizophrenia and other serious mental health conditions.

Throughout his career in psychiatric hospitals and correctional institutions, Jerry began questioning conventional explanations for auditory hallucinations. Based on his experiences with patients, he developed a controversial theory that some of the voices associated with schizophrenia may originate from external, potentially parasitic entities rather than being purely products of the brain.

We explore the disturbing patterns he claims to have observed, the relationship between negative voices, fear and emotional distress, and why he believes traditional psychiatric approaches fail to address the underlying phenomenon.

In this conversation, we explore:

- Are the voices heard by people with schizophrenia simply hallucinations?
- Why do some voices appear hostile, manipulative or threatening?
- The similarities between psychiatric symptoms and historical accounts of demonic possession.
- Jerry's experiences working with patients who reported hearing voices.
- His controversial techniques for challenging and confronting these voices.
- How the psychiatric community has responded to his theories.
- What these experiences might reveal about consciousness and the nature of reality.

Could some experiences traditionally classified as mental illness point toward something we don't yet fully understand?

Join us for a fascinating and controversial discussion that challenges conventional thinking about the human mind, consciousness and the boundaries of reality.

Disclaimer: The views expressed by the guest are his own and do not represent established scientific or medical consensus. Schizophrenia is a recognized psychiatric condition, and there is no reliable scientific evidence that it is caused by demonic entities. This conversation is intended for discussion and exploration, not as medical advice or a substitute for professional mental health treatment.

videos.title: Prime Winter Loamy Gold At Dalby Forest
videos.description:
Dalby Forest in the thick of November isn't supposed to ride this good, but we were blessed with primo loamy gold conditions, minimal mud and smiles for miles. If you love loamy berms, steep technical sections and fast flowing woodland singletrack, this is a mountain biking spot you need on your list!

In this video we start on a fresh loamer track not far from the visitor centre. It's steady as you go, which was the perfect first trail of the day to get into it and dust off the cobwebs.

After a swift climb we hit Tranny Temps, with a sneaky steep exit off the normal trail. Another swift climb led us down Deere's Dungeon, a steep descent with a few spicy log drops towards the bottom.

Then after a bit of a push away from the woods we hit Loose for Lewis, a much longer trail to test the lungs. It was running prime with everything you want: tech, flow and steep sections to tickle your MTB pickle.

Next comes probably my favourite trail at Dalby, Monster Munch. With over 13 berms back to back we were pinning it down the hillside at rapid pace. It's a must ride if you're in these woods!

Another swift climb led us back up the hill to S**t and Spade, which was flowy with spicy sections to test your skillset, especially the back to back drops at the end and the steep off camber shoot towards the start.

After a detour up a red route climb we hit two absolutely dreamy loamer tracks, with the forest floor lit up by golden loam. These two felt special, and I think they're called Tom and Rockin Robin on Strava, so if anyone can confirm that in the comments it would be appreciated.

The shuttle run was next, with insane flow and sniper roots to catch you off guard. The last trail before heading back was Scarborough Fair, with rapid flow through the autumnal leaves before dropping into the spicy stuff at the bottom, with gap jumps and drops. This one was insane.

The final two trails were back where we started. First a full run down the fresh loamer, trying to open up the taps after taking it steady earlier in the day, then the nearby Corkscrew, which follows the same trail in parts but has a much steeper end and was the perfect wrap up to a dreamy day at Dalby.

Whether you're after berm after berm, spicy drops or golden winter loam, Dalby Forest is well worth the trip for any mountain biker visiting North Yorkshire!

ST Engineering’s order book has reached SGD 37.7 billion, but its nine-month update gives no profit figure. For dividend investors, a record backlog is not the same as income you can count on.

videos.title: 10 Habits of Successful Investors That Build Wealth Over Time / Successful Stock Market Investors
videos.description:
#stocks #stockmarket #investing #shares #NSE


What separates successful investors from those who struggle to build wealth in the stock market? It is not always how much money they have, how intelligent they are, or whether they can predict where stock prices will move next. Often, it comes down to their habits, behaviours and investment discipline.

In this video, we explore 10 important habits of successful investors that can help you become a better investor, make smarter financial decisions and build sustainable wealth over time.

Whether you are investing in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), exploring other investment opportunities in Kenya, or building a long-term investment portfolio, these behaviours can significantly influence your investment journey.

HERE ARE THE 10 HABITS WE DISCUSS:

1. Investing consistently - Building the discipline to invest regularly instead of waiting for the perfect opportunity.

2. Doing research before buying - Understanding a company's business, financial performance, growth prospects and valuation before investing.

3. Thinking long-term - Understanding that meaningful wealth creation takes time, patience and consistency.

4. Controlling emotions - Avoiding decisions driven by fear, greed, panic or excitement when stock prices fluctuate.

5. Protecting investment capital - Prioritising capital preservation, managing risk and avoiding investments that could expose you to permanent losses.

6. Reinvesting investment returns – Using dividends and investment gains to grow your portfolio through the power of compounding.

7. Continuously learning - Improving your knowledge of businesses, financial statements, stock valuation and investment opportunities.

8. Having an investment plan - Establishing clear financial goals, an investment strategy and a defined investment horizon.

9. Thinking independently - Avoiding herd mentality and making investment decisions based on research rather than popular opinion.

10. Practising patience and discipline - Understanding when to invest, when to wait and why doing nothing can sometimes be the best investment decision.

THE BIGGER LESSON:

Successful investing is not about getting rich overnight. It is about developing the right behaviours, making sound financial decisions repeatedly and allowing time and compounding to work in your favour.

If you want to become a better stock market investor and build lasting wealth, start developing these habits today.

videos.description:
Thank you so much for watching! It means the world to me that you enjoy my content! If you don't already, please like, subscribe and comment to help out my channel. You can also find me on facebook as Patty Workman, also on IG and Tik Tok as Workman Racing and Adventures. If you really want to help me out, I'm monetized on FB, so watching, liking and commenting there actually earns me some $$. Thanks again for watching!

First race of the season is always an exciting and intimidating event. How will I stack up against the new guys in my class? Have I regressed or progressed since the last time? Will my fitness hold out? Big question... Will I get hurt? Let's face it, racing is dangerous. Way more dangerous than trail riding. Especially for us since we mostly just fuck around and don't ride fast. We're just out there enjoying the moment, the scenery, and mostly avoiding getting hurt. We're too old for that and we don't have time for that LOL. 

Before the race I told myself I was NOT going to go for it. I was going to take it easy, play it safe. I'm not chasing points. We're only doing a few races this season. However, once that race starts, all bets seem to be off. 

We had 9 in our class. I got a good start, and quickly found myself in 2nd. I held that until a traffic jam at a tree, then had to take my fogging googles off and found my way back to 4th. That's when I finally settled in. I was basically cool with a 4th out of 9. At the beginning of the 3rd lap Matt went down hard and cracked a rib, so he was out. If you don't watch the whole thing, you at least have to find that part. It's kind of funny. This landed be back in 3rd, where I finished. 

I'm quite happy with how it went. The conditions were super slick and after Matt got hurt, I certainly couldn't afford to get hurt as well. I rode as well as I feel like I could have, so that was awesome. My fitness was on point. I never got tired. I certainly held my own in the class. The 2 guys that finished in front of me were in the 30 class last year and one of them won the class in '25. Matt probably would have beat me, but he usually does, so I'm used to it, LOL. Besides it feels really cool to be married to a 62 yo dude who can win or at least hold his own in the 40 yo class!

videos.title: 5 portfolio Mistakes Stock Investors Make - Portfolio Investing Tips for Stock Market Investors
videos.description:
#Stocks #stockmarket #investing #portfolio #shares #nse


You can buy good stocks, invest in profitable companies and even identify great investment opportunities, but still end up with a poorly performing stock portfolio.

Why? Because successful stock investing is not just about choosing the right companies. It is also about how you construct, diversify and manage your investment portfolio.

In this video, we explore 5 costly portfolio mistakes that stock market investors make and how to avoid them.

Here are the five mistakes we discuss:

1. OVERCONCENTRATION – Putting too much money into one stock or company. Even a fundamentally strong company can experience difficulties, and excessive exposure to one investment can put your entire portfolio at risk.

2. POOR DIVERSIFICATION – Owning several stocks but investing heavily in the same sector. Having 10 or 15 stocks does not automatically mean you have a well-diversified portfolio. Understand how your investments are distributed across different sectors and industries.

3. INVESTING WITHOUT A CLEAR STRATEGY – Buying stocks simply because they are cheap, popular or recommended by someone else. Every investment should have a purpose and fit into your broader investment objectives.

4. IGNORING PORTFOLIO REBALANCING – Failing to review and adjust your portfolio as market prices, company fundamentals and investment opportunities change. Your portfolio should evolve as your investment circumstances change.

5. FOCUSING ON INDIVIDUAL STOCKS INSTEAD OF OVERALL PORTFOLIO PERFORMANCE – A few winning stocks do not necessarily mean you have a successful portfolio. You need to evaluate your overall returns, losses, dividends, costs and portfolio risk.

THE BIG INVESTMENT LESSON:

Stock picking is only one part of successful investing. Building a balanced portfolio, managing risk and periodically reviewing your investments are equally important.

Whether you are investing in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), international stocks or building a long-term investment portfolio, avoiding these mistakes can help you become a more disciplined investor.

Issuing $244.7 million of common MSTR shares via at-the-market (ATM) sales at depressed prices dilutes existing equity holders.

Adding 485 BTC at roughly $68,866 per coin lowers the overall average cost basis and increases Bitcoin-per-share over a multi-year horizon. With BTC trading below Strategy's $75,452 average cost, the company is sitting on roughly $8.9 billion in unrealised paper losses, amplifying downside volatility.


Index & Market Flows 
Passive outflows from index removals often create temporary mis-pricings that reverse once forced selling clears. Forced institutional selling ahead of MSCI index removals at the end of November creates a predictable near-term overhang.


Portfolio & Risk Evaluation Framework

Because Strategy uses convertible debt, preferred stock, and common equity issuance to fund its treasury, it behaves differently from holding spot Bitcoin directly.
